_comment: The pre-registration of agent_architecture.md §7's last reporting rule: budget
and hyperparameters are fixed before any test run, all method debugging happens
on train, and every arm is reported on test — never 'best of'. Committed before
the registered search and before any test rollout; its sha256 travels with every
run (harness/preregistration.py), so an edit after the fact moves the hash rather
than quietly redefining what was promised. Amendments are appended to
'amendments' with their reason, never applied by rewriting a value in place.

supersedes.what_it_produced: eval/measurements/20260826T164850Z.json — the T134 run, two arms × three splits × three repeats, complete
why_a_third_one: T134 answered its own question and the answer was null. On test_seen, the
primary estimand moved +0.011 [+0.000, +0.032] on the answer metric against a
baseline of 0.818; trajectory +0.037 [-0.032, +0.128]; card recall +0.047
[+0.000, +0.140]; the aggregated selection score +0.017 [-0.008, +0.046]. On
test_unseen both arms scored 1.000 on every metric, 6 templates tied and 1 had
no data. §8 states the suite detects differences on the order of 20 percentage
points; every one of those is an order of magnitude below it.
The run itself was sound, which is what makes the null worth acting on. §7's
repeat condition did NOT fire this time — residual exclusions converged between
the arms (test_seen 43 vs 39 of 375, test_unseen 66 vs 65 of 168, train 1 vs 0
of 300) where P8c's diverged 14 vs 25 — so the comparison is established rather
than merely recorded, and 'the optimizer found nothing' is a result and not an
artifact of the measurement.
What that result CANNOT distinguish is the thesis question from a ceiling. The
seed is the handwritten baseline: 30,296 characters of routing rules, a
tool-result taxonomy, a caveat list and six fully documented tool declarations,
written by hand against this exact catalog. It enters at 0.818 answer accuracy
on test_seen and 1.000 on test_unseen. An optimizer that finds nothing on top of
that has either failed, or has been handed a prompt with nothing left in it —
and T134 cannot tell a reader which.
This registration separates the two by moving the seed, not the optimizer.
Everything about the search, the budget, the models, the suite and the analysis
is held at registration 2's values; the seed's ROUTING content is cut back to a
bare inventory of names, and the run is read for whether the same optimizer at
the same budget recovers it. A gain here says the search works and T134 measured
a ceiling. A second null says the search does not work on this testbed, and says
it against a seed that demonstrably had room.

commit_note: T134's tip, and the branch point of `headroom-weakened-seed`. It carries the
two thought-part fixes, the request timeout, the hard provider pin and T135's
The weakened seed and this registration land in the ONE commit after it, and
no rollout of this registration exists against either. Naming the branch point
rather than that commit is what registration 2 did and for the same reason: a
registration cannot carry the hash of the commit it is inside.
registered_against.case_files_note: Byte-identical to registrations 1 and 2. The suite is NOT re-drawn: the whole design of this run is that one thing moved, and a redrawn suite would be a second thing.

what_this_registration_is: THE ONE THING THAT MOVED. Registration 2 measured an optimizer against a strong
seed and found nothing. This one measures the same optimizer, at the same
budget, against a deliberately weak seed, so that 'nothing to find' and 'cannot
find it' stop being the same number.
It is a HEADROOM experiment and it is labelled one. The baseline arm here is not
the assistant anyone would deploy and its numbers are not a claim about the
assistant; they are the floor the gain is measured from.

candidate_surface_chars.note: Registered prompt template lengths, version 6/7 (registration 2's seed) → version 9/10 (this one's).

what_was_cut: From the root instruction: the 'Which tool answers what' routing section, the
'What a tool result means' taxonomy of the three tool outcomes, and the
'Caveats you must carry into explanation' list. 3,751 characters replaced by a
324-character section naming the six callables and saying that each one's own
From each of the five function-tool docstrings: the self-containment rule, the
per-argument guidance, the scope limits, the returned-field glossary and the
disclosure instructions. What remains is a signature paraphrase — argument
names, types and the shape of the return.
The result is a seed that still says WHAT exists and no longer says WHEN to
reach for it, which is the routing knowledge §7's trajectory metric scores and
the knowledge a prompt optimizer is supposed to be able to rediscover.
what_was_deliberately_not_cut: THE ANSWER CONTRACT, byte-for-byte. Everything from '### How you answer' down to
the `explanation` bullet — 1,553 characters — is identical to the text every
earlier run used, as is the site preamble above it. It is what parse_contract
reads and what makes a status scorable, so it is measurement apparatus and not
the thing under test. Weakening it would turn every rollout into a
`parse_failure` and the run would measure the harness.
THE NO-CLARIFICATION CLAUSE, which sits inside that block. §8's ambiguity
residual rests on the candidate never asking a question back, and the abstention
metric rests on a two-valued status.
T136's callable-naming sentence, in all six tool texts: each says it is the
declaration of the tool it declares and names the callable. T134 showed the
proposer using it to repair the `agent_tool_` confusion that broke P8c's winner,
and T137 — the missing check on a candidate naming a callable no toolset
resolves — is still not landed, so this sentence is the only thing standing
between the search and that failure mode.
`lookup_reference`'s topic enum, which lives in the function signature and not
in the docstring (§3.2), so ADK renders it into the declaration regardless. The
weakened text names no topics; the model still receives the eleven card keys.
The sub-agent's outward description, unchanged at 217 characters. It was already
a name and a subject line — there was nothing in it to cut, and its sha256 is
the one candidate pin this registration does not move.
what_this_cannot_show: A gain here is a gain FROM A WEAK SEED and does not transfer to the strong one.
The two runs bracket the question rather than answering it jointly: T134 bounds
what the optimizer adds to a hand-written prompt, this one bounds what it
recovers from a stripped one, and the true value of the technique on an
arbitrary prompt lies somewhere between and is not measured by either.
The weakening is one draft by one author, not a sampled degradation. How much
headroom it actually opened is not known until the baseline arm is measured, and
if the baseline lands near 0.818 anyway then this run has produced a second null
with a smaller excuse rather than a contrast.
Cutting the docstrings changes the token count as well as the content: the
candidate surface fell 84%, so the baseline arm's rollouts are cheaper and
shorter. Any diagnostics comparison with T134 reads against that and not only

unchanged_from_registration_2: The model id, the endpoint, the decoding parameters and the one-model-in-both-
roles deviation below. Holding them fixed is what makes the seed the only thing
why_gmicloud_and_not_deepinfra: The provider is pinned with allow_fallbacks=false on all three paths (the ADK
rollout, the text-to-SQL chain's bare litellm calls, GEPA's reflection call) —
registration 2's amendment 1, unchanged in mechanism. What moved is WHICH
provider, and it moved because registration 2's amendment 2 recorded deepinfra's
pool answering `engine_overloaded` in bursts, which a hard pin cannot reroute
around and which cost that run a stopped-and-restarted search.
gmicloud answered cleanly at 4.2 s mean in the screen, against deepinfra's 4.4 s
— the same order, with no observed overload burst.
This is a SECOND thing that differs from registration 2, and it is registered
as such rather than folded into the seed change. It is not chosen on any test
number: the screen below ran on throwaway prompts and no split was touched.

provider_screen.note: Carried forward so no later session re-runs it. Screened on the three failure modes registration 2's amendment 1 named: reasoning leaked into `content`, rate limits, and latency.
provider_screen.deepinfra: clean, 4.4 s mean — registration 2's pin; dropped for `engine_overloaded` bursts under a hard pin (registration 2, amendment 2)
provider_screen.relace: cheapest, therefore the router's default preference, and unusable: inlines the chain of thought into `content`, which is where the SQL builder reads its query
provider_screen.open-inference: clean but 40–55 s mean — turns this run into days

one_model_in_both_roles: REGISTERED DEVIATION from §5, carried forward unchanged from registration 2. §5
asks for a reflection model distinct from the model under test so a result can
be attributed to one of the two; here they are the same served model on the same
endpoint, so the search is a model reflecting on its own rollouts and this run
cannot separate 'the proposer is weak' from 'the task model is weak'.
It matters MORE to this registration than it did to the last one. T134's null
was already ambiguous between a weak proposer and an exhausted seed; this run
removes the second ambiguity and leaves the first. A null here still admits 'the
proposer is this model, reflecting on itself'. That is the stated limit of what
a second null would establish, and it is registered before the number exists.
The pins stay two separate slots, so the choice is recorded rather than lost.

budget.available_note: Derived: registration 2's 23.25 less this repository's own ledger for that run (4.11). It is the repository's arithmetic, not a balance read from the provider.

basis: Registration 2's MEASURED spend at this model's rates rather than an estimate:
its registered search cost $1.006 over 567 rollouts, its smoke search $0.015
over 10, and its eighteen measurement conditions $3.086 — $4.11 against a
limit of 6.0, so registration 2's own estimate of 4.4 was a good one.
The seed is 84% shorter, and prompt tokens dominate a rollout at ~21k mean, so
the baseline arm should come in UNDER this. The optimized arm will not: a
proposer rewriting a stripped docstring writes a longer one, and a model with
less routing guidance takes more steps. The limit is unchanged at 6.0 because
the estimate is a floor in both runs and the headroom is what absorbs it.
The ledger's metric is labelled `cost_eur` and the prices are USD. That is the
repository's label, noted rather than fixed inside a registered run.

budget.if_exhausted: The split order in `measurement.splits` decides what is lost, exactly as registration 1's amendment 3 decided it and registration 2 kept it. Registered before any test rollout and on no test number.

baseline: THE WEAKENED SEED at the pinned candidate_prompt_versions — root instruction v9,
the five tool docstrings at v9/v10, the sub-agent description at v9 — registered
once and read twice, so the reference arm and the search's seed cannot drift
apart. `seed_weakening` above is the whole of what makes it different from
It is NOT comparable with registration 2's baseline arm and no difference
between the two is reported as an effect. Reported side by side, as two seeds,
which is the entire point of running it.
It is expected to score WORSE than registration 2's baseline on the routing-
bearing metrics, and it is registered before that is known. If it does not, that
is the finding — it would mean the tool declarations were never load-bearing and
the model was routing off the callable names and the ADK schema all along, which
is a result about the testbed and is to be reported as one rather than repaired.
optimized: Whatever candidate the one registered search selects. Not the best of several
searches, not the best iteration by test score, not a hand-picked candidate:
the search's own selection, on the aggregated scalar, over train alone.
The search starts FROM the weakened seed, which is what makes the pair a
measurement of recovery rather than of addition.

search.gepa_kwargs_note: Registration 2 registered `{}` here and its search duly reported a deviation naming the digest it actually ran. The digest is registered outright this time, so a deviation line means the metaprompt moved rather than that the registration was incomplete. T136's proposer-side change is inside this digest and is unchanged from T134.
budget_held_fixed: 500 metric calls, the same number registration 2 ran. A weaker seed is a reason
to WANT a larger budget and precisely the reason not to take one: a gain bought
with more rollouts would not be comparable with T134's null, and comparability
with T134 is what this run is for.
llm_cache_hygiene: `.cache/llm` is CLEARED before the registered search. The response cache is
keyed on the request and not on the serving provider, so a smoke run against a
different provider replays its answers into the registered run under a matching
key. Registration 2's provider pin is what made this reachable and nothing in

measurement.pairing: the identical committed cases, in file order, for every arm and every repeat
repeats_note: Three, unchanged. The three repeats ARE the replication and are what makes the
LLM response cache's being off matter: a prompt-keyed hit would hand the first
repeat's bytes to the other two. T134 measured 0.135 of test_seen cases
disagreeing across their repeats in BOTH arms, which is the noise floor this

why_it_is_not_widened_again: T134 lost 43 and 39 of 375 test_seen rollouts and 66 and 65 of 168 test_unseen
rollouts to `upstream`, nearly all of it cache misses on windows a candidate
chose. That test_unseen rate — around 39% of rollouts in both arms — is high
and is the largest standing threat to what this run can say about the holdout.
It is NOT widened here. The counts converged between the arms, which is the
property §7 actually reads, and widening the neighbourhood would move a second
thing between the two registrations while the whole design is that one moved.
It is registered as a known cost instead, and §7 still publishes the per-arm
count and reads each arm's against the other's rather than against zero.
A weakened seed may well choose WIDER windows than a guided one, so the miss
rate is expected to rise in the baseline arm and possibly to diverge between the
arms. If the counts diverge, §7's repeat condition fires and this run is
repeated rather than reported — registered here, before the counts exist.

analysis.repeat_reduction: mean over the repeats per case, before any aggregation over cases
analysis.primary_estimand: the paired difference optimized - baseline, per metric, on test_seen
analysis.test_unseen_trajectory: per-template win/loss table; no accuracy and no interval
analysis.abstention: accuracy over the unanswerable cases and the false-abstention rate over the answerable ones, reported separately and never blended
analysis.exclusion: harness_error cases leave every aggregate and are counted per arm with their sources broken out; invalid_argument never excludes
parse_failure: Reported apart from answer accuracy, and it carries more weight in this run than
in any before it. The contract block was preserved precisely so that a weakened
seed degrades ROUTING and not FORMAT; a non-zero parse_failure count in the
baseline arm would mean the weakening reached the contract after all and that
the arms differ in the apparatus rather than in the thing measured. T134 ran
0.000 in every condition. Any non-zero count here is reported before any other
number and bounds what the rest of the run means.
analysis.residual_nondeterminism: MEASURED, from the three repeats per condition. Every arm difference is read against it, and a difference smaller than it is reported as within the noise floor rather than as a small effect.
analysis.multiplicity: no correction across the four metrics. They are four declared quantities, not a family searched over for a winner; the interval and the noise floor carry the uncertainty and the suite is stated to detect large effects only
comparison_with_registration_2: REPORTED SIDE BY SIDE, NEVER POOLED AND NEVER DIFFERENCED, on the same terms
registration 2 set for P8c. Two things moved between the runs — the seed and the
serving provider — so no single difference between them is attributable to one.
The comparison is between two GAINS, not between two baselines and not between
two optimized arms. T134's gain on test_seen answer was +0.011 [+0.000, +0.032]
from a seed of 0.818. This run reports its own gain from its own seed, with both
seeds' absolute scores stated so a reader can see the headroom each had.
The qualitative questions carried across are: whether the exclusion counts stay
converged between the arms, whether parse_failures stay at zero, and whether the
direction of the answer metric's movement reproduces. None is given an interval.
what_a_null_would_mean: Registered before the number exists, because a null is the outcome this design
is most likely to be accused of explaining away afterwards.
If the baseline arm scores materially below registration 2's 0.818 and the
optimized arm does not recover it, that is evidence the search does not work on
this testbed — bounded by the two declared gaps (T132's missing span half, the
one-model-in-both-roles deviation) and by the suite's own 20-point sensitivity.
If the baseline arm scores at or near 0.818 despite an 84% cut to the candidate
surface, the finding is about the TESTBED and not about the optimizer: it would
mean the optimizable text was never carrying the routing, and that §7's
trajectory metric is scoring something the callable names and the ADK-rendered
schema already determine. That is a publishable negative result about the
instrument and is to be reported as one.
Neither outcome licenses a fourth registration that weakens the seed further
until a gain appears. One weakening, registered, reported whatever it gives.

method_debugging: train only. The two test splits have been run under registrations 1 and 2 and
their numbers are in findings.md, so — as with registration 2 — this is not
written by someone who has never seen a test number.
Nothing in it is chosen on one. The seed weakening is driven by an ambiguity in
T134's null that §7's own reporting made visible; the provider change is driven
by an error class registration 2's amendment 2 recorded; the budget, the suite,
the splits, the repeats, the bootstrap and the analysis are copied unchanged
precisely so that neither can be tuned against a number.
reporting: Both arms on all three splits, whatever the numbers are, and labelled a headroom
experiment wherever they appear. The baseline arm is a deliberately degraded
prompt and its absolute scores are never quoted as the assistant's performance.
§7's repeat condition applies unchanged: residual failure counts diverging
between arms mean the arms were not measured under the same conditions and the
run is repeated. Diverging newly-recorded cache entry counts are reported and
stopping: The measurement is complete when both arms have three repeats on all three
splits. It is not stopped early on a favourable interval, and it is not extended
on an unfavourable one. One search, one measurement, one report.

known_gaps.what: The reflective dataset reaches GEPA without its span half: MLflow stands down from tracing when ADK is already tracing, so the search reflects on `Feedback.rationale` and the inputs, and not on the ADK tool spans.
known_gaps.status: NOT FIXED in this run. tasks.md orders it before a rerun and it is not landed; the run proceeds with it declared rather than waiting.
known_gaps.effect: The proposer sees less about a rollout than the design intends. It weakened registrations 1 and 2 equally and weakens this one the same way, so it does not confound the comparison — but it bounds a null harder here than it did there, because this run's whole claim rests on the proposer being able to rediscover routing it can only infer from rationales.

known_gaps.what: The proposer is asked to rewrite, not to revise, and nothing checks a candidate that names a callable no toolset resolves. P8c's winner is what that produces: one tool description rewritten into a root-agent system prompt naming `agent_tool_predict_green_roof_water_balance_tool`, which does not exist.
known_gaps.status: NOT FIXED in this run. tasks.md orders it before a rerun and it is not landed.
known_gaps.effect: A candidate of this run may be broken the same way and nothing will refuse it. The risk is HIGHER than in T134: a stripped docstring invites wholesale rewriting where a full one invites editing. T136's sentence inside each tool text is the seed-side half that IS landed and T134 showed the proposer using it to self-correct. Any candidate naming a callable outside TOOL_NAMES is reported in findings.md by hand for this run.

known_gaps.what: test_unseen lost about 39% of its rollouts in both arms of registration 2 to `upstream` cache misses, on a split of only seven templates.
known_gaps.status: NOT REPAIRED here, by choice — see `capture.why_it_is_not_widened_again`.
known_gaps.effect: test_unseen supports description and not inference in this run either, which §7 already required of it for a different reason. Its win/loss table is read as such.
